spec.requirement: The daemon serves the v1 REST contract of specs/openapi.yaml: /health, /api/v1/sessions, /api/v1/stats, /api/v1/metrics, POST /api/v1/search, POST /api/v1/chat. Non-v1 paths (/api/sessions, /api/flows, /api/search, /api/chat) return 404. With RABBITHOLE_API_KEY set, every protected route requires the key and exactly /health plus the two metrics paths stay public (auth.go noAuthPaths).
spec.acceptance: Live probe of a hermetic server: all six v1 routes answer 200, all four non-v1 routes answer 404, protected routes answer 401 without the key and 200 with it, /health answers 200 without the key (foreman row DF-020, commit 419aaca).
spec.verification: Go tests: internal/express/auth_test.go, internal/express/server_test.go, cmd/rabbit-hole/execution_test.go (daemonClient routing). Machine-checked citation deferred (RH-TOOLING-001).
spec.requirement: Chat over REST matches the CLI: with a model loaded both answer non-time-window questions from recorded flows; without a model both return the stub answer with stub:true. LLM cold starts do not surface bare 500s: the client timeout is configurable (RABBITHOLE_CHAT_MODEL_TIMEOUT, default 120s), a warm-up runs at serve start, timeouts retry once and answer 503 with a structured retryable error body (foreman row DF-035, commit ca4516c).
spec.acceptance: A mock slow LLM endpoint yields 503 + retryable message within the configured timeout, never a bare 500; the CLI surfaces the structured message. Dogfood friction F3 (REST chat dead-ending where CLI chat answers) is closed or explicitly re-scoped.
spec.verification: Go tests: internal/express/chatmodel_test.go, internal/express/chat_test.go, cmd/rabbit-hole/chat_test.go. Machine-checked citation deferred (RH-TOOLING-001).
spec.requirement: The CLI never opens its local DB path when talking to a daemon: status, list, search, compact and demo all accept --addr and route through the daemon HTTP API (foreman rows DF-014/GAP-007), so a differing RABBITHOLE_DB_PATH between server and CLI can never show phantom data. The daemon's own DB path is what status prints.
spec.acceptance: Live scenario: serve on /tmp/a.db, attach with /tmp/b.db in the environment, then `list --all` shows the daemon's session and `status` prints the DAEMON's DB path — never the CLI's (foreman row DF-014 live verification).
spec.verification: Go tests: cmd/rabbit-hole/list_test.go, cmd/rabbit-hole/status_test.go, cmd/rabbit-hole/compact_test.go, cmd/rabbit-hole/demo_test.go. Machine-checked citation deferred (RH-TOOLING-001).
